source_name: Mastercard Česká republika – Tiskové centrum
why_relevant: Mastercard's Czech-language press centre — the counterpart to Visa CZ for contactless share, tokenisation, wallet and merchant-acceptance announcements. Returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and a browser-UA curl, which is characteristic of Akamai/edge bot defence rather than a dead page; the domain is still linked as live from Czech trade sites. Treat as bot-defended-but-live and unverified.

source_name: Mastercard global newsroom – press releases
why_relevant: Mastercard's global press feed, reachable when the Czech localised site is not. Carries Europe-wide scheme changes (tokenisation mandates, click-to-pay, instant-payment and open-banking moves) that propagate to CZ. Note: only /news/insights/, /news/perspectives/, /news/press/ and /news/terms-of-use/ were visible in the navigation — no country-level newsroom path was found, and www.mastercard.com/news/europe/cs-cz/ returns 403.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – statistiky českého kartového trhu
why_relevant: The Czech Bank Card Association publishes the only long-run, scheme-neutral CZ card dataset: quarterly and annual PDF + XLSX files covering cards in issue, cashless transaction counts/values, ATM withdrawals, cashback and e-commerce, with a consolidated history file back to 1989 and series from 2000-2026. Terminology and methodology manuals are published alongside. This is the reference series against which Visa/Mastercard marketing claims can be sanity-checked.

source_name: CardMag.cz – česká odborná platforma o platebních kartách
why_relevant: Czech card-industry trade publication, evidently run by the same circle as SBK (it mirrors the SBK statistics charts and the same TZ archive). Useful as a curated secondary feed that flags which scheme announcements the Czech industry itself considers notable, plus event coverage (Prague Payments Week, CardSession, Acquiring Day). Has an English mirror at /pages/eng/home_e.html.

source_name: Bank iD (Bankovní identita, a.s.) – Pro média
why_relevant: Press hub of the bank-owned national digital-identity operator. Publishes Czech-language press releases on public-sector and private use cases (land registry, school admissions, driving-licence renewal), plus downloadable factsheets carrying headline adoption numbers (cited as ~5.3m users, ~80% of the working-age population). Bank iD is the identity rail that CZ banks jointly own, so its releases signal where bank-issued identity is being monetised next. PR contact published on-page.

source_name: Bank iD – Články / novinky (blog)
why_relevant: Higher-frequency companion to the press page: product launches, new relying parties, sector adoption commentary. Typically the first place a new Bank iD integration or feature is described in Czech.

source_name: Bank iD – Pro akcionáře (shareholder / general meeting materials)
why_relevant: Statutory shareholder page of the bank-owned operator. Currently thin — one general-meeting package (September 2026) as a ZIP — and notably it does NOT host an annual report or financial statements. Still worth monitoring because general-meeting materials disclose capital changes and new shareholder banks joining the identity scheme.

source_name: Bank iD – Developer portal (technická dokumentace)
why_relevant: Technical documentation and changelog for the Bank iD scheme. Spec/scope changes (new claims, new authentication levels, sign-service features) usually land here before any marketing announcement, making it a leading indicator of identity-rail capability shifts.

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin – Bankovní identita, a.s. (IČO 09513817)
why_relevant: Because Bank iD does not publish an annual report on its own website, the statutory Collection of Deeds (Sbírka listin) at the Ministry of Justice is the only route to its audited financial statements, annual reports, shareholder structure and board changes. Registered office confirmed as Smrčkova 2485/4, Libeň, 180 00 Praha 8. The same registry serves any Czech-incorporated scheme or infrastructure entity in this cell.

source_name: ARES – Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (REST API)
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance registry with an open REST API that resolves Czech legal names to IČO and registered address — the entity-resolution layer for this cell (confirmed Bankovní identita, a.s. = IČO 09513817). Feeds the Sbírka listin lookup and disambiguates the many similarly named payment entities.

source_name: European Payments Council (EPC) – SEPA scheme owner
why_relevant: Owner and rulebook publisher for the SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD Core, SDD B2B, Request-to-Pay, One-Leg Out) and of the register of scheme participants, in which Czech PSPs appear. Directly relevant to CZ because euro instant-payment obligations bite in 2027 and Czech banks adhering to SCT Inst show up in that register. Note the old domain www.epc-cep.eu now 301-redirects here; deeper paths (/what-we-do/sepa-payment-schemes, /document-library) returned 403 to automated fetches, which reads as bot defence rather than removal.

source_name: ECB Data Portal – Payments statistics (PSS dataset)
why_relevant: Harmonised EU payments statistics including Czech Republic series on card payments, terminals, acceptance and payment-system throughput, compiled from ČNB reporting. Gives a cross-country comparable denominator that neither ČNB's Czech-only pages nor scheme marketing provide, and supports contactless/e-commerce share benchmarking against CEE peers.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – Pro média
why_relevant: The Czech Banking Association is the collective voice of CZ banks on scheme-level topics (instant payments, SEPA migration, fraud prevention, identity) and is repeatedly cross-linked from Czech card-industry sites. Useful as a pointer to industry positions and to working groups that sit between the banks and CERTIS/Bank iD. Overlaps with a banking-association cell if one exists — deduplicate on ingest.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide, Inc. – Investor Relations (NASDAQ: EEFT)
why_relevant: Parent-level disclosure for the Czech market's largest non-bank ATM deployer. Quarterly results and the EFT Processing segment carry active-ATM counts, transactions per ATM, and commentary on European ATM network expansion/rationalisation and surcharge/DCC economics — the parent numbers are the only recurring, timely quantitative frame around the Czech fleet, which the local entity discloses only annually via statutory filings.

source_name: SEC EDGAR – Euronet Worldwide (EEFT) 10-K / 10-Q filings
why_relevant: Statutory US filings are the most auditable parent-level disclosure for Euronet's independent ATM business. 10-K risk factors, segment notes and geographic revenue tables are where country-level exposure, ATM fleet totals and regulatory/fee risk (incl. European surcharge and DCC regulation) are stated under liability. Full-text search lets you pull every mention of 'Czech' across years.

source_name: Loomis Czech Republic a.s. – Czech corporate site (cz.loomis.com)
why_relevant: Local site of one of the two dominant cash-in-transit / cash-management operators in Czechia (IČO 26110709, Praha – Horní Počernice, also listed at Sezemická 2853/4). Documents the service portfolio actually sold into Czech banks and retail — přeprava hotovosti (CIT), zpracování hotovosti, ATM servicing, retail cash solutions — and a 'Místa' (locations) page that reveals the cash-centre footprint, which is the practical proxy for national cash-logistics capacity.

source_name: Loomis AB – Investor Relations, annual & interim reports (Nasdaq Stockholm)
why_relevant: Swedish listed parent of Loomis Czech Republic. Annual & Sustainability Reports, quarterly interim reports and Capital Markets Day decks give the group view on CIT volume trends, cash-in-transit pricing, ATM outsourcing and 'Loomis Pay'/SafePoint penetration in Europe. Even without a Czech line item, group Europe commentary sets the direction of travel for the Czech subsidiary and flags M&A that would reshape the Czech CIT duopoly.

source_name: Brink's Czech Republic (brinks.cz) – site & 'Novinky a blogy'
why_relevant: Local site of the other dominant Czech cash-handling operator (Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) a.s., IČO 27590151; Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) s.r.o., IČO 08829969; both at Na Košince 2257/9, Praha 8 – Libeň). Uniquely for this cell it runs a genuine Czech-language content stream covering the strategically important shift from classic CIT to smart safes / Digital Retail Solution (DRS) and outsourced ATM operation ('Správa a obsluha ATM'), plus an EV fleet programme and an announced partnership with G4S Secure Solutions (CZ) a.s. Those posts reveal service-model change and competitive positioning that never appear in bank disclosures.

source_name: The Brink's Company – Investor Relations (NYSE: BCO)
why_relevant: US-listed parent of the Czech Brink's entities. 10-K/10-Q and quarterly decks carry Europe segment organic growth, ATM Managed Services (AMS) and Digital Retail Solutions revenue lines — the group metrics that explain what Brink's is pushing into the Czech market, and the vehicle through which G4S cash-business acquisitions were disclosed.

source_name: Obchodní rejstřík / Sbírka listin (or.justice.cz, verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz) – statutory filings of Czech ATM and CIT operators
why_relevant: This is the single highest-value disclosure channel for this cell. Czech deployers and CIT firms are private subsidiaries with no local IR, so their audited účetní závěrka / výroční zpráva reaches the public only through the court-run Sbírka listin. Confirmed live entries with a Sbírka listin link: Euronet Services, spol. s r.o. (IČO 25608452, C 54449 Městský soud v Praze, founded 1997-09-16) and Loomis Czech Republic a.s. (IČO 26110709, B 17852, registered 2006-11-01). Same route applies to Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) a.s. (27590151) and Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) s.r.o. (08829969). Yields revenue, headcount, related-party fees to parent, and sometimes ATM-fleet or contract commentary in the annual report narrative.

source_name: ARES – Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (REST API, ares.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Machine-readable state registry that resolves and normalises every Czech legal entity in this cell — legal name, legal form, seat, NACE/CZ-NACE activities, registration status across ROS/VR/RES/RZP/DPH. Verified working in this run for Euronet Services, spol. s r.o.: returns IČO 25608452, DIČ CZ25608452, Pobřežní 620/3, Karlín, 18600 Praha 8, established 1997-09-16, all registers AKTIVNI. It is the reliable spine for entity resolution before pulling Sbírka listin documents, and its CZ-NACE codes let you sweep for *all* firms registered for cash-handling/security-transport activities, not just the ones you already know.

source_name: Czech company-data aggregators (Chytrý rejstřík, Finmag rejstřík, Podnikatel.cz rejstřík, Měšec rejstřík firem, Živéfirmy)
why_relevant: Fast triage layer over the register: pre-parsed revenue bands, headcount, ownership chains and document counts without pulling PDFs. Confirmed for Euronet Services: revenue band 300–500 mil. Kč (ČSÚ, 2024), 10–19 employees, 100% owned by EFT Services Holding B.V. (Amsterdam) since June 2015, 56 documents in Sbírka listin, plus counts of register changes and public contracts. The tiny headcount against a 300–500m CZK revenue is itself a finding — it evidences how far the Czech ATM estate is operationally outsourced to CIT partners.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam úspěšně otestovaných zařízení pro zpracování bankovek / mincí
why_relevant: A regulator-maintained equipment registry that is unusually revealing for self-service intelligence: to be used for processing Czech banknotes/coins under Act 136/2011, a device model must pass ČNB testing and appear on these lists. That makes the lists a de-facto census of the ATM, recycler, deposit-module, sorter and coin-handling models legitimately deployable in Czechia, naming the manufacturers behind the Czech self-service estate. Changes in the list are an early signal of vendor entry, model refresh and recycling/deposit capability spreading through the fleet.

source_name: ČNB – Legislativa k oběhu bankovek a mincí + gov.cz reporting duty for cash processors
why_relevant: Defines the compliance perimeter every Czech cash-handling firm operates inside: the Act on the circulation of banknotes and coins (136/2011 Sb.) and its implementing decrees, mandatory professional courses for cash handlers, and — via the gov.cz service catalogue — the statutory duty of persons processing domestic banknotes and coins to report to ČNB. That reporting duty implies a supervised population of cash processors and a data flow worth pursuing (including by information request), and the training/decree changes are leading indicators of cost pressure on CIT operators.

source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek (vvz.nipez.cz) – public tenders for cash transport and ATM services
why_relevant: Statutory Czech tender bulletin. State bodies, municipalities, hospitals, transport operators and state enterprises procure CIT, cash processing and self-service/ATM placement here, and award notices name the winning operator and the contract value. This is one of the few places where Czech cash-logistics pricing and counterparties become public at all, since bank–CIT contracts are private. Award notices also reveal capability claims and regional coverage of bidders.

source_name: NEN / Zakázky GOV (zakazky.gov.cz) and tender aggregators (tendry.cz)
why_relevant: The national electronic procurement tool where many CIT and self-service tenders are actually run end-to-end (documentation, bids, awards), complementing the Věstník's notice-level view. Tender documentation often contains the operational detail that matters for this cell — number of collection points, frequency of servicing, ATM models to be serviced, SLA and insurance limits — which is otherwise unobtainable.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – bankovnikarty.cz, Czech card & ATM market profile
why_relevant: The Czech card-industry association (founded 1992) historically published the market's canonical ATM, POS and card series — ATM counts, transaction volumes and withdrawal values — which is exactly the fleet denominator this cell needs, and it counts the whole estate rather than only bank-operated machines. Value is now qualified: the detailed series on the profile page still run to ~2011–2012 even though the page carries a recent update stamp, so treat it as a historical baseline plus an actor/pointer to member institutions rather than a current-data feed.

source_name: CardMag (cardmag.cz) – Czech payment-cards and self-service trade magazine with PDF archive
why_relevant: Specialist Czech trade title for the cards/ATM/self-service industry with a downloadable back-issue archive. Trade press of this kind is where deployer network deals, ATM vendor wins, CIT contracts and fleet numbers get named before (or instead of) appearing in any formal disclosure, and the archive gives a long time series for reconstructing how the Czech ATM estate and its outsourcing model evolved. Primary use is as a snowballing pointer to actors, product names and events.

source_name: Peníze.cz – ATM directory (bankomaty v ČR) and network/fee reporting
why_relevant: Combines two things this cell needs: a searchable national ATM directory with addresses and maps (a practical basis for estimating and geo-profiling the estate, including deployer-operated machines), and sustained reporting on network economics — the launch of 'the largest ATM network in Czechia', shared deposit ATMs going live for three banks, and Euronet extending surcharges to Czech cards. Useful both as fleet-mapping raw material and as an event feed.

source_name: Czech business/news media ATM tag feeds (Seznam Zprávy, Newstream, banky.cz, CzechCrunch, iDNES, Aktuálně, iROZHLAS)
why_relevant: General and business media carry the network-structure stories that neither regulators nor operators publish on a schedule: banks negotiating a further shared deposit-ATM network, the four-bank shared network launch, and public controversy over Euronet's surcharging (including a viral consumer campaign and an MEP intervention that Euronet publicly rebutted). Tag feeds give cheap, dated event capture across the whole cell and reliably name the participating institutions.

source_name: Policie ČR – press releases on ATM attacks and cash-in-transit crime
why_relevant: ATM physical attacks (solid/gas explosive attacks, ram raids) and CIT robberies are a direct driver of deployer and bank economics: they push operators toward gas-suppression, ink/glue staining, deposit-only or lobby-sited machines, and they are a stated reason for fleet reduction in exposed locations. Police releases give dated, located, quantified incidents that no commercial source aggregates for Czechia, and a senior officer has publicly characterised attacks as running to dozens.

source_name: KPKB ČR – Komora podniků komerční bezpečnosti ČR (kpkbcr.cz) and allied security associations
why_relevant: Sector chamber for commercial security businesses (founded January 1993) with corporate and individual member directories, a magazine, guard-qualification exam material and downloadable organisational documents. Cash-in-transit in Czechia is legally and operationally part of the commercial-security industry, so this chamber and its partner bodies (Česká komora služeb ochrany majetku a osob, Grémium Alarm, Česká asociace bezpečnostních manažerů, Hospodářská komora ČR) are the route to enumerating smaller and regional CIT/valuables-transport firms that no financial-sector list captures. Note: the partner page did not list Loomis/Brink's/Securitas, so membership coverage of the large CIT players is unconfirmed.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Czech Republic (dnpilsen.cz / Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o.) and other self-service vendors with Czech operations
why_relevant: The vendor layer beneath the Czech self-service estate. Diebold Nixdorf runs a substantial Czech operation (a Pilsen global centre, several hundred staff per its recruitment material) and Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o. is a registered Czech entity; NCR/NCR Atleos and legacy Wincor Nixdorf equipment is also present in the field. Vendor sites, Czech job postings and the local entity's own statutory filings are the practical way to read service-contract scale, managed-services push and which technology generation the Czech fleet is on — none of which appears in bank or deployer disclosures.

source_name: Czech crypto-ATM operators and manufacturer (General Bytes, Bitperia, CryptoATM, bitcoinmaty.cz)
why_relevant: An adjacent but genuinely relevant part of the Czech self-service cash ecosystem: a domestic manufacturer/operator base (General Bytes, described in Czech media as among the world's largest producers and operators of bitcoin ATM infrastructure, and reported hacked in 2023) plus operating networks (Bitperia, CryptoATM, bitcoinmaty.cz). These machines compete for the same high-footfall cash-accepting sites as bank and deployer ATMs, are a live cash-in/cash-out channel, and are the population most exposed to incoming AML/MiCA-driven registration duties — a regulatory front that will reshape non-bank self-service in Czechia.

source_name: Česká pošta, s.p. – cash and payment services at post offices (incl. cash withdrawal) and annual reports
why_relevant: Czech Post is a large non-bank cash-access and cash-handling network (SIPO, poštovní poukázky, the ČSOB Poštovní spořitelna counter partnership, and a cash-withdrawal-from-account service), and as a state enterprise it publishes annual reports and appears in the public contracts register. Its counter network is the main substitute channel when bank branches and ATMs are withdrawn from small municipalities — the same demand gap Euronet targets with its 'ATMs for obce' offer — so its service and pricing changes are a leading indicator for deployer opportunity.

source_name: ATM location directories and POI datasets (banky.cz, Mapy.com/OSM, Firmy.cz)
why_relevant: The only practical bottom-up way to size and profile the Czech ATM estate by operator, since neither ČNB (bank-operated only) nor SBK (stale) publishes a deployer-level breakdown. banky.cz maintains per-bank ATM listings with addresses; Mapy.com and Firmy.cz carry large numbers of individually tagged 'Bankomat Euronet' and bank ATM POIs (including OSM-sourced entries), which supports operator-mix and regional-density estimates and detects new deployments and removals over time.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (cbaonline.cz) and ČBA Monitor
why_relevant: The Czech Banking Association publishes surveys, indices and sector positions, and ČBA Monitor carries sector data. For this cell it is a secondary but useful channel for branch/ATM accessibility positions, cash-availability policy debate and fraud statistics that contextualise self-service investment; it is also the natural venue in which any industry-level position on shared ATM infrastructure or cash access obligations would be voiced.

source_name: Trask — Financial Services industry hub (thetrask.com)
why_relevant: Trask is one of the largest Czech banking-IT integrators. Its financial-services hub names bank clients (Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, Slovenska sporitelna) and describes delivered systems (Impresto digital lending, Data-In Open Banking Connector, payments). Because Czech systemic banks are private and never tender publicly, this vendor page is one of very few public records of what technology those banks actually bought. It also carries quantified claims (e.g. a stated share of CZ/SK online payment volume touched by Trask expertise) that can be tracked over time.

source_name: Trask — Insights / case-study and blog index
why_relevant: The running index where Trask publishes named bank project write-ups. Observed entries cover J&T Bank digital-channel rebuild, MONETA real-time customer engagement on AWS Kafka/Flink, Raiffeisenbank logging/observability, and a Verification of Payee (VOP) build with Banfico. Case studies and blog posts share the same /blog/<slug> URL space, so a single crawl captures both announcement-grade and technical-detail content. This is the highest-yield single index in the cell for CZ bank technology projects.

source_name: Monet+ — Reference (Czech-language client case studies)
why_relevant: Monet+ (Zlin-Stipa) is the Czech specialist in banking digital identity (ProID) and card/transit payment acceptance (Switchio). Its Czech-language reference list explicitly names CSOB (EMV card acceptance in public transport), Ceska sporitelna (securing Servis24/Business24 internet banking; PKI smartcard network access) and Air Bank (secure internet-banking access). These are concrete, dated public traces of security and payment-acceptance decisions inside private Czech banks that appear nowhere else.

source_name: Monet+ — Novinky (Czech newsroom) and product lines ProID / Switchio
why_relevant: The Monet+ homepage nav exposes 'Novinky' alongside the two product franchises that matter for this cell: ProID (qualified signatures, certificate lifecycle for banks and insurers) and Switchio (EMV, tokenisation, transit and EV-charging acceptance). Named institutional relationships visible at homepage level include Komercni banka (with an on-record quote from the head of direct-channel development), Raiffeisenbank, Erste Group, PPF and Kooperativa. Tracking the newsroom catches new bank wins before they reach trade press.

source_name: Profinit — Case studies index (banking-heavy)
why_relevant: The densest bank-project disclosure found anywhere in this cell. Individually addressable case studies name Komercni banka (BI partner), Raiffeisenbank (three separate projects: AI campaign targeting, big-data stack, instalment detector), Equa Bank (interest-rate optimiser), Ceska sporitelna (fraud-detection platform), Erste Group Bank (central log monitoring) and M.M.Warburg. Each is effectively a public record of an analytics/risk/fraud programme inside an otherwise opaque private bank, and the Equa Bank item is useful historical evidence given Equa's absorption into Raiffeisenbank CZ.

source_name: Profinit — Financial Services industry page and Blog/News
why_relevant: Client-logo wall and positioning page carrying KBC, Erste Group, KB (Komercni banka), Raiffeisen Bank and Berenberg. The logo wall is a cheap, high-signal way to detect new bank relationships (a logo appears before any case study does). The paired /blog/ index adds commentary that often previews regulatory-driven build programmes (DORA, instant payments, VoP).

source_name: Adastra — Success stories (EN and CS)
why_relevant: Adastra's portfolio sitemap exposes a banking-heavy success-story set: a robotic branch assistant at Tatra banka, automatic categorisation of ~98.5% of card transactions, Raiffeisenbank internet-banking response-time work with Dynatrace, an unnamed 'leading bank' data-management concept, MetLife paperless applications, and event-driven marketing in banking. Crucially, every story exists in a Czech mirror under /cs/success-stories/, so this satisfies local-language coverage for Adastra. The anonymised 'leading bank' items are themselves intelligence: they signal deals the bank refused to be named in.

source_name: Aricoma — Our customers, Banks & Insurance filter
why_relevant: Aricoma (KKCG technology division, ~EUR 500m revenue, 6000+ staff) publishes a filterable customer wall with an explicit 'Banks and Insurance Companies' branch. Named financial customers observed: CSOB Group, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, ING Management Services, Citibank, plus Kooperativa, UNIQA, Simplea, Home Credit, Broker Consulting and SATUM. For the largest Czech integrator this customer wall is the only systematic public statement of which banks it serves, and Aricoma is a roll-up so the wall changes as it acquires.

source_name: Aricoma — Tiskove zpravy (Czech press releases)
why_relevant: Full Czech-language mirror of the Aricoma newsroom (URL pattern /cs/tiskove-zpravy/<slug>, EN mirror at /press-releases/<slug>). This is the disclosure channel for Aricoma's M&A and, when banks permit it, for named bank projects. Recent output observed is M&A-dominated (Dentsu Tracking acquisition 01/08/2026; SAP suppliers in Austria and Slovenia 08/01/2026; SAP consolidation 01/01/2026) which is itself relevant: it maps how Czech bank-IT supply is consolidating under KKCG.

source_name: KKCG — Investors and Group news (Aricoma's parent)
why_relevant: KKCG is an investment group (stated 40+ countries, EUR 1.5bn+ EBITDA, 16,000+ employees) whose Technology division contains Aricoma. Because Aricoma itself is not separately listed, the parent's investor disclosures and news feed are the closest thing to audited, periodic reporting on the largest Czech bank-IT integrator — division revenue, acquisitions and strategy. The news feed exposes a machine-readable RSS endpoint.

source_name: ICZ Group — Reference (incl. CEBIS for Ceska exportni banka)
why_relevant: ICZ's Czech-language reference section carries a filterable 'Bankovnictvi' / 'Pojistovnictvi' vertical. The concrete banking reference observed is CEBIS, a bespoke commercial-case origination and approval system for CEB (Ceska exportni banka) covering loans, guarantees, purchased receivables and syndicated/club deals — a rare public description of an origination platform at a state-owned Czech bank. Adjacent insurance/pension references (Dovera, VsZP, Union, STABILITA) map ICZ's document-management franchise across CZ/SK financial institutions.
